investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-05T05:40–05:47Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never started.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (peer-pod / confidential-VM slots) had no remaining allocatable capacity, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received an agentId or vmId, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (requiring vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]) could not be satisfied. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: harness-health eval fails: /api/agents/harness/health returns an error payload missing the required `status` evidence key due to absent LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN
investigation.summary: The harness-health eval check failed because the API endpoint /api/agents/harness/health returned an error object instead of a valid JSON health payload, leaving the required evidence key `status` absent from the collected evidence. The raw evidence captured by the runner contains an explicit error message — "hosted local harness requires LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN" — confirming the harness service rejected the request before it could produce a health response with a `status` field.
investigation.rootCause: The harness service at https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com requires a LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN credential to respond to health requests. When the eval runner called GET /api/agents/harness/health, the harness rejected the request and returned an error payload that contained `reachable: false`, `url`, and an `error` string, but no `status` field. Because the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 353) requires `status` as mandatory evidence, the contract validation failed. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the harness-health check; no user-traffic or production-incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.evidence: raw evidence contains { reachable: false, url: 'https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com', latencyMs: 0, error: 'hosted local harness requires LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN' } — the `status` key is entirely absent.
failed-check.message: contract validation error is 'Missing expected evidence: status'.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: verifier confirms `status` is the sole missing required evidence key.
expected-output.contract: check-expectations.json lines 351-359 require requiredEvidence: ['reachable', 'status', 'url'] and assert status equals 200.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1524-1532: runner at line 1531 calls apiJson(args, 'GET', '/api/agents/harness/health') and returns { evidence: health } verbatim — if the health response is an error object without a `status` key, the contract gap is introduced here.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=135 and evidence latencyMs=0, consistent with an immediate auth rejection rather than a network timeout.

sibling.marketplace-agents: the sibling check marketplace-agents passed with evidence key `count`, confirming the broader marketplace-bootstrap feature and production-api runtime are reachable; the failure is isolated to the harness-health check.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN is not configured in the eval runner environment: the harness service requires this token and immediately rejects unauthenticated requests with an error payload that lacks a `status` field, directly causing the missing-evidence contract failure (supported by failed-check.evidence error string).

SECONDARY — The harness service at https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com is returning a non-standard error envelope (containing `error` instead of `status`) when authentication fails, and the runner passes this envelope directly as evidence without normalizing or extracting an HTTP status code (supported by source-context run-status-probes.mjs line 1532: `return { evidence: health }`).

TERTIARY — The eval runner's token guard at line 1530 (`if (!args.token) return { status: CHECK_STATUS.SKIP, ... }`) guards against a missing args.token but does not guard against a valid token that is rejected by the harness itself, meaning a misconfigured or expired LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN would bypass the skip path and still reach the failing API call.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-05T05:40–05:47Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never started.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (peer-pod / confidential-VM slots) had no remaining allocatable capacity, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received an agentId or vmId, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (requiring vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]) could not be satisfied. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod was never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads or leaked/zombie VMs, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not satisfy the pod's node selector, which may reflect a correct constraint (only kata nodes can run peer-pods) or a misconfigured label that is excluding nodes that should be eligible.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 kata-capable nodes, which may be insufficient for the current workload demand plus observability probe traffic.

Lower probability — a leaked or stuck remote-agent VM from a prior eval run is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883, reducing available capacity.

investigations.title: harness-health eval fails: /api/agents/harness/health returns an error payload missing the required `status` evidence key due to absent LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN
investigations.summary: The harness-health eval check failed because the API endpoint /api/agents/harness/health returned an error object instead of a valid JSON health payload, leaving the required evidence key `status` absent from the collected evidence. The raw evidence captured by the runner contains an explicit error message — "hosted local harness requires LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN" — confirming the harness service rejected the request before it could produce a health response with a `status` field.
investigations.rootCause: The harness service at https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com requires a LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN credential to respond to health requests. When the eval runner called GET /api/agents/harness/health, the harness rejected the request and returned an error payload that contained `reachable: false`, `url`, and an `error` string, but no `status` field. Because the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 353) requires `status` as mandatory evidence, the contract validation failed. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the harness-health check; no user-traffic or production-incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
